metadata.headline: How does Walmart turn retail scale into marketplace power?

platform_lesson.title: Retail assets can become platform infrastructure
platform_lesson.text: Walmart Marketplace is stronger than a standalone digital marketplace because it can combine third-party seller supply with assets Walmart already built for retail: consumer trust, stores, fulfillment, data, payments and advertising reach. Sellers expand assortment and generate referral-fee and advertising opportunities, while Walmart's physical and digital infrastructure can improve delivery, returns and customer confidence. The strategic challenge is to scale third-party supply without allowing seller quality, logistics or trust problems to weaken the Walmart brand that attracts demand in the first place.

core_value_unit.explanation: The Product Listing is the unit of value made discoverable through Walmart Marketplace: a seller's offer combining the product, price, availability, delivery promise and other information a Shopper uses to decide whether to buy.

actor.explanation: Price-conscious shoppers, families and online buyers use Walmart Marketplace to compare and purchase products from Walmart and third-party Sellers through one customer experience.

job.explanation: Shoppers use the marketplace to find products that meet their needs at competitive prices without having to search across many separate retailers.

gain.explanation: A wider assortment, competitive prices, convenience and the Walmart brand can reduce the effort and perceived risk of online shopping.

pain.explanation: High prices, weak selection, delivery problems or uncertainty about third-party seller quality can reduce the value of the marketplace for Shoppers.

transaction.explanation: Shoppers place an order and pay through Walmart's checkout even when the underlying product is offered by a third-party Seller.

filter.explanation: Participation can be constrained by account rules, fraud controls, age or product restrictions and the ability to use Walmart's digital channels.

access_channel.explanation: Shoppers reach the marketplace primarily through Walmart.com and the Walmart app, while Walmart's physical stores can support pickup, returns and other parts of the experience.

activities.explanation: Shoppers search and compare listings, place orders, pay, receive or pick up purchases and can leave reviews that feed back into marketplace trust.

resources.explanation: Shoppers contribute attention, purchase intent, account and payment information, device access and the behavioral data created through their marketplace activity.

actor.explanation: Third-party sellers, small businesses and brands supply additional assortment to Walmart Marketplace without Walmart owning that inventory.

job.explanation: Sellers join Walmart Marketplace to reach Walmart's customer base without having to build an equivalent consumer marketplace themselves.

gain.explanation: Marketplace participation can provide additional demand, brand exposure, sales scale and performance data while giving Sellers access to Walmart's commerce infrastructure.

pain.explanation: Sellers compete for visibility and price while also managing inventory, fulfillment, returns, customer service and marketplace performance requirements.

transaction.explanation: Sellers supply products to Shoppers through Walmart Marketplace and pay Walmart referral fees on completed sales; fee rates vary by category.

filter.explanation: Walmart requires business verification, compliant products, marketplace or e-commerce experience, valid product identifiers, returns capability and adherence to seller performance standards.

access_channel.explanation: Sellers manage the marketplace through Seller Center, direct APIs or approved solution providers, depending on their technical setup.

activities.explanation: Sellers create and optimize listings, manage price and inventory, fulfill orders directly or through Walmart services, handle support and maintain marketplace performance.

resources.explanation: Sellers contribute product data, inventory, pricing, fulfillment capability, seller credentials and the operational capacity required to serve Walmart customers.

actor.explanation: Logistics firms, advertising and technology providers, payment services and other solution partners extend capabilities that Walmart or Sellers can use around the marketplace transaction.

job.explanation: Service Partners help make marketplace transactions work at scale through fulfillment, integrations, payments, advertising and other specialist services.

gain.explanation: A large marketplace can generate recurring demand, transaction volume, customer reach and revenue opportunities for external service providers.

pain.explanation: Service Partners have to cope with technical integration, demand peaks, quality expectations and the operational requirements of participating in Walmart's ecosystem.

transaction.explanation: Partners provide logistics, technology, payment or advertising services and receive commercial compensation through their contracts or service relationships.

filter.explanation: Partners must meet Walmart's technical, operational and quality requirements; services that cannot scale or meet compliance expectations can lose access.

access_channel.explanation: Service Partners typically connect through APIs, direct business integrations, contractual relationships and operational dashboards rather than the shopper-facing marketplace interface.

activities.explanation: Partners integrate their systems, deliver services, maintain service quality and scale capacity as marketplace transaction volume changes.

resources.explanation: Partners contribute logistics infrastructure, software and data interfaces, specialist teams and service-level commitments.

actor.explanation: Walmart Inc. owns the marketplace environment and its marketplace team governs how third-party Sellers and supporting services participate.

metrics.note: Walmart reported U.S. Marketplace sales growth of approximately 20% in Q4 FY26.

job.explanation: Walmart's job is to expand marketplace assortment and transaction volume while maintaining the customer experience and economics of the broader Walmart ecosystem.

gain.explanation: Marketplace growth can expand assortment and customer loyalty while adding referral-fee, advertising and service revenue opportunities without Walmart owning every item sold.

pain.explanation: Rapid seller growth can create quality, counterfeit, compliance, customer-service and technology-scaling problems that may damage trust in the Walmart brand.

transaction.explanation: Walmart sits inside the marketplace transaction: it collects customer payment, deducts category-based referral fees and coordinates settlement or payout to Sellers, while also monetizing services such as advertising.

governance.explanation: Walmart governs entry and participation through product policies, business verification, seller performance standards, reviews, compliance controls, dispute processes and enforcement.

promotion_channel.explanation: Walmart can promote marketplace demand through its website, app, search visibility, advertising, email, social channels and physical store presence.

activities.explanation: Walmart recruits and onboards Sellers, monitors quality and performance, promotes listings and marketplace services, coordinates transactions and scales the platform infrastructure.

resources.explanation: The marketplace draws on Walmart's brand, digital platform, commerce data, seller support, marketing reach, legal and policy capabilities, payment infrastructure and physical retail network.

current.explanation: Shoppers place marketplace orders and pay through Walmart's checkout.
Walmart coordinates seller settlement after the marketplace transaction, net of applicable fees and adjustments.
Sellers pay Walmart category-based referral fees on completed marketplace sales.
The Seller provides the product that fulfills the Shopper's marketplace purchase, directly or through a fulfillment service.
Walmart can contract and pay external service partners for logistics, technology, payments, advertising or other marketplace capabilities.
Service Partners can support the Shopper-facing transaction through delivery, payments or other enabling services.

metrics.note: Walmart reported U.S. Marketplace sales growth of approximately 20% in Q4 FY26.
